key: Behold, I have refined thee, but not as silver; I have tried thee in the furnace of affliction.
s: Midway through a rebuke of obstinate Jacob, spared for the sake of God’s name; Radak, on 48:10, reads it as a refining short of the silversmith’s, who removes all the dross, since then few would have remained, the wicked being afflicted but not cut off.

evidence.gloss: But not as silver: not like a refiner of silver, for the refiner removes all the dross from the silver and consumes it until nothing but refined silver is left; I did not do so, for few would have remained had I done so; but the wicked among you, who are the dross, I afflicted with sicknesses, captivity, bereavement of children, or in the fruit of cattle or of the ground, as written in the curses, not to cut them off altogether.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, Isaiah 48:10, at [381,10]). Plain sense faithful: 48:1 to 8 rebukes Jacob as obstinate and treacherous, 48:9 defers anger for the sake of God’s name so as not to cut him off; no four-word repeat. Radak on 48:10 (Hebrew, packet) says God did not refine as the silver refiner does, removing all the dross, since few would have remained, but afflicted the wicked (the dross) without cutting them off altogether; the reading paraphrases exactly that, without drift. Rashi and Metzudat David read the furnace of poverty or servitude in place of the fire of Gehinnom, and Ibn Ezra the exile; Radak’s reading is distinct and his own. Entry-check ok.
